steps: Prepare the existing fireplace
Confirm a clean, non-combustible chimney in good order; block the damper open or remove it and remove the chimney cap. Drill a gas access hole if needed and fit the conversion warning label.

Approved for masonry and factory-built solid fuel burning fireplaces. Any removed parts must be capable of re-installation (removing rivets or screws is acceptable).

  • Clean the chimney and fireplace to keep creosote odor out of the home. Verify mantel and sidewall clearances (Section 8.0).
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and log grates may be removed.
  • Factory-built fireplace with no gas access hole: drill one of 1½ in. (37.5 mm) or less through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox; plug it with non-combustible insulation once the gas line is in.
  • Provide electrical power; the electrical access location is on Figure 2.1 (p. 9).
  • Mechanically attach the label warning that the fireplace is converted for a gas insert only, at the bottom of the existing firebox.
Cut the liner & fit the cap
Cut #816 to the measured chimney length and extend both pipes. Intake pipe over cap collar (A), exhaust pipe sealed onto collar (B), each with (3) self-tapping screws.

1. Measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney and subtract the insert height (p. 12). Cut #816 (36' [10.97m] of 3" flexible pipe) to that length.
  2. Carefully extend the exhaust and combustion air intake pipes to the total length.
  3. Slide the combustion air intake pipe (the end without a collar) over cap collar (A); secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).
  4. Bead sealant around the inner edge of the exhaust pipe end, slide it onto collar (B), secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided) and seal the joint.

Install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right. Avoid tight bends that can abrade or damage the flex pipe.

Note: the #816-CAP drawing on p. 15 labels the sealant "not provided"; the vent-run and adapter steps on pp. 17 and 18 say "sealant (provided)".
Run the liner down the chimney
Slide the vent adapter out of its channels. Feed the 3" x 3" flex down the chimney, seal and set the cap, then pull both pipes into the firebox.

1. Remove the vent adapter by sliding it back out of the channels on top of the appliance.
  2. Optional: wrap unfaced insulation around the first 3 ft (914 mm) below the cap and secure with wire.
  3. Lower the pipes down the chimney. With offsets, guide them with a weighted rope around the pipe ends; never tie one rope around both pipes.
  4. Run a liberal bead of sealant around the top of the chimney and set the cap per the vent manufacturer's instructions. #816-CAP option: 2 in (50 mm) self-tapping screws and anchor straps (not provided) through the side pilot holes.
  5. Pull the pipes down until both the exhaust pipe and combustion air intake are in the firebox.

Insulating the pipes and chimney with unfaced insulation listed noncombustible per ASTM E 136 helps prevent cold air drafts and heat loss.
Connect the adapter & seat the insert

Exhaust (red marking) inside the "Exhaust" collar, intake over the intake collar, each sealed with (3) ½ in self-tapping screws. Slide the insert in, pull the adapter forward until seated and secure it.

1. Place the vent adapter in the fireplace opening. Seal and slide the exhaust pipe inside the collar marked "Exhaust"; seal and slide the intake pipe over the intake collar. Secure each with (3) ½ in (13 mm) self-tapping screws and add sealant for an airtight joint.
  2. Slide the insert in until the channels on top align with the adapter.
  3. Pass the pull rod handle through the access slot on top and hook it into the pull rod. Push the insert in while pulling the adapter forward until seated.
  4. Secure the adapter through the top slots with (2) ½ in (13 mm) sheet metal screws (components packet). Use the pull rod handle to pull the adapter back to its starting position, remove the handle and verify the vent connection.
  5. Level if needed with the leveling bolts (2 each side).
Gas line connection
Listed ½ in. tee handle shut-off and flexible connector to the ½ in. control valve inlet, run through the right-side hole clear of the fan. Leak-test every joint with soapy water.

• Install by a qualified person to local codes, or ANSI Z223.1; in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Supplied: 3/8" (10 mm) x 18" (457 mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • In a minimum-size opening the gas line may need to be run after placement.
  • Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve for system tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at or below, close its manual shut-off valve.
  • Propane: manufactured for natural gas; convert with the kit and its instructions before installing the logs.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water (p. 29).
Shroud & safety barrier
Lift out the upper and lower louvers and remove the glass. Fix the shroud to the cabinet's mounting nuts with (4) truss head screws, refit the parts, then hang the barrier in the shroud slots.

1. Lift the upper louver up and out of its mounting flanges; lift the lower louver out of the slots on its bracket.
  2. Remove the glass assembly (p. 27; never while hot).
  3. Align the shroud's holes with the mounting nuts on the sides of the insert cabinet (2 each side) and secure with (4) truss head screws (provided).
  4. Reinstall everything removed.
  5. Safety barrier: align the tabs on its back with the (4) shroud slots (2 each side), raise it slightly into the slots and let the tabs drop into place. To remove, lift it up and out.
Trim panels or surrounds must not seal the existing fireplace's ventilation openings, and draft relief openings must not be covered. For a low mantel, fit the CK29-LMK heat deflector to a CK29-RSF or CK29-PSF barrier (p. 24).
Install the log set
Finish any propane conversion first. Ember panel in front of the burner, base logs CK29-1 to CK29-4 onto the burner pins, the top logs into their notches, then rock wool embers.

1. Position the ember panel in front of the burner.
  2. Align the holes in base logs CK29-1, CK29-2, CK29-3 and CK29-4 with the burner's mounting pins and push them down to seat.
  3. Align logs CK29-5 and CK29-8 with the notches in the base logs and ember panel.
  4. Align the notches in logs CK29-6 and CK29-7 with the log grates on the burner.
  5. Distribute rock wool embers onto the logs and burner.
Never place logs directly over burner port holes: improper placement may affect flame appearance and build soot on the glass. Log numbers are on the bottom of each log.
Wiring & controls
Plug into a grounded three-prong receptacle. The millivolt valve needs no 110-120 VAC; an optional thermostat or wall switch runs on low-voltage wire to the TH and TP-TH terminals.

• Optional thermostat or wall switch: run low-voltage wires from the gas valve to the control and connect them to the top and bottom terminals marked TH and TP-TH. The wire assembly is not included. Mount the control on a wall near the fireplace.
  • Either disconnect the rocker switch wires from the back of the valve, or leave the rocker switch OFF. If it is ON, the burner runs until the rocker switch turns it off; the wall switch or thermostat can't.
  • Never connect high voltage (115V) wire to the gas valve.
  • Outdoor covered installs: wiring to the outdoor requirements of NECA NFPA 70 (p. 19).

The two wiring schematics (rocker switch; thermostat or wall switch) are drawings on p. 31.
Gas pressure test
With every other gas appliance on, check inlet at the IN tap and manifold at the OUT tap with a ¼ in I.D. hose. Retighten each tap snug and confirm it reads no pressure.

Inlet (IN tap, A)

  1. Loosen the IN tap screw counterclockwise and attach the manometer with a ¼ in (6 mm) I.D. hose.
  2. Light the pilot and turn the knob to ON. The burner should not light. Note the reading.
  3. Press the rocker switch ON and check the pressure is near maximum inlet pressure. Rocker switch OFF, then knob OFF.
  4. Disconnect, tighten the screw clockwise (snug, not over tight), relight the pilot, knob to ON and reattach: the tap should read no pressure.

Manifold (OUT tap, B)

Light the pilot, loosen the OUT tap, attach the manometer, knob to ON, rocker switch ON and note the reading. Retighten snug and confirm no pressure with the rocker switch ON.

Inlet NG / LP5" – 10.5" WC / 11" – 13" WC
Manifold NG / LP1.6" – 3.5" WC / 6.4" – 10" WC

Inlet too high or too low: contact the gas company. Only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure; low pressure can cause a delayed ignition.
Burner flame check
Flames start blue and gradually turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. The venturi is factory set; any adjustment is for a qualified service technician, in slight increments.

Venturi, natural gas3/16" (4.8 mm) open
Venturi, propane5/8" (16 mm) open

If soot is on the glass, check log positions first: logs must not block burner ports. To adjust, remove the safety barrier and glass frame, then the log set and burner assembly; loosen the venturi screw, adjust, re-tighten and reinstall. Slight changes give dramatic results: burn at least 15 minutes and let the unit cool before adjusting again.

Dark orange, black tipsVenturi closed too far · open slightly
Short, blue flamesVenturi open too far · close slightly
Lifting (ghosting)Gas pressure too high or venturi closed too far · check manometer, open slightly
Note: p. 35 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner (Table 12.3: close the venturi slightly for short, blue flames); the troubleshooting chart on p. 37 says a flame that burns blue and lifts off the burner may need the venturi opened slightly.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: No spark: piezo igniter wiring loose or not grounded, or electrode gap not 1/8 in (3 mm)
Sparks but no pilot: no gas. Check for multiple shut-off valves in the supply line, or an empty propane tank
Pilot flame not impinging on the thermocouple: clean the pilot hood, adjust the pilot flame
Loose thermocouple (hand tight plus 1/4 turn); reading below 15 millivolts: replace it
Thermopile below 350 millivolts at TH-TP and TP: replace it. Frequent outages: pilot shield missing, or pilot flame too high or low

panels.title: Burner won't light or stay lit
items: Knob not at ON, rocker switch not ON, or no heat demand from the wall switch, remote or thermostat
Defective switching device: jumper the switch terminals, then the gas valve terminals
Thermopile wires loose at the valve, or pinched and grounding out
Refractory panels (if installed) not tight against the firebox walls

panels.title: Pilot and burner go out while running
items: Improper pitch on horizontal venting: the chart says ¼ in (6 mm) per 12 in (30 cm); pp. 15 and 16 say a 1 in rise per 12 in
Inner vent pipe leaking exhaust back into the firebox, or vent cap blocked

panels.title: Glass sooting or lifting flames
items: Sooting: venturi may need opening slightly
Blue flames lifting off the burner: the manual's venturi advice conflicts (pp. 35, 37)
Incorrect vent cap installation, vent cap blocked, or vent pipe leaking

light.title: Lighting the pilot
light.html:
You light the pilot by hand at the gas valve with the piezo igniter button. Read the safety steps first. To reach the knob, remove the safety screen and open the lower grille.

  1. Set any thermostat to its lowest setting and turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  2. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
  3. Wait five minutes for any gas to clear. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you do, stop and follow the gas-smell steps.
  4. Find the pilot: follow the metal tube from the gas control into the combustion chamber.
  5. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counterclockwise to PILOT.
  6. Push the knob in all the way and hold it. Press the piezo button repeatedly until the pilot lights.
  7. Keep holding the knob for one minute, then let go. It pops back up and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, start again at step 2.
  8. Turn the knob counterclockwise to ON. Close the grille, refit the screen, restore power and set the thermostat.
Stop and call your service technician or gas supplier if the knob doesn't pop back up, or if the pilot won't stay lit after several tries (turn the knob to OFF first). Use only your hand on the knob, never tools.

To shut the gas off

Set the thermostat to its lowest setting, push the knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF.

burner.title: Turning the flames on and off
burner.html:
With the pilot lit and the gas control knob at ON, the main burner is switched on and off with the ON/OFF rocker switch. Your installer may also have added a wall switch or thermostat.

Which control is in charge

  • To use a wall switch or thermostat, leave the rocker switch at OFF (unless your installer disconnected it).
  • If the rocker switch is ON, the burner keeps running until you turn the rocker switch off. The wall switch or thermostat can't turn it off.

Burner won't come on?

Check that the gas knob is at ON and that the rocker switch is ON, or that your wall switch or thermostat is calling for heat. Anything beyond that is a job for a qualified technician.

Power

The millivolt gas valve doesn't need 110-120 VAC house power to operate. The fireplace does have a three-prong grounding plug: plug it straight into a properly grounded three-prong outlet, and never cut or remove the grounding prong.

To shut off the gas to the fireplace completely, turn the gas control knob to OFF. The steps are under Lighting the pilot.

height.title: Setting the flame height
height.html:
Your Chaska 29 MV has a manual HI/LO knob on the gas valve. It sets both the flame height and the heat output.

  1. Remove the safety screen and open the lower grille to reach the gas valve.
  2. Turn the HI/LO knob clockwise toward HI or counterclockwise toward LO.
  3. Stop when you like the flame and the heat.
  4. Set the grille back in place and put the safety screen back on.
Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never run the fireplace without the safety screen in place.

The rated input is 18,500 to 28,500 Btu/h on natural gas and 22,000 to 29,000 Btu/h on propane.

sounds.title: First fire: what's normal
sounds.html:
Foggy glass

When you first light the fireplace, condensation appears on the glass. This is normal in all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during that time; it helps the paint cure faster.

Noises as it heats and cools

The metal expands and contracts, so the fireplace can make noises of varying degree. This is normal and doesn't affect how well it works or how long it lasts.

Blue flames at first

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes of operation they gradually turn yellow.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building, and leave. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass once a year. Do it only when the glass is cool, never while it's hot.

  1. Set up a flat, stable work surface big enough to hold the glass assembly.
  2. Remove the safety screen. Pull the two spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down, then lift the glass assembly up and off the two tabs at the top.
  3. Clean the glass with a suitable fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  4. Refit the glass: set the slots at the top over the tabs, lower the bottom into place, and pull the latches out and up to secure it.
  5. Put the safety screen back. Don't run the fireplace without it.
Don't run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. Avoid striking or slamming the glass. A licensed or qualified service person should replace it, with the complete glass assembly from Hussong Mfg. (#701-009T). Wear protective gloves to handle broken glass.

timeout.title: The 7-day pilot time-out
timeout.html:
Some regions require a 7-day time-out. For those installations, the Chaska 29 MV is fitted with a millivolt Pilot-on-Demand gas valve with a 7-day timer. Ask your dealer whether yours has one.

How it works

  • The timer starts when you light the pilot.
  • Any time the main burner lights during the next 7 days, the timer resets to 7 days.
  • If the fireplace isn't used for 7 days in a row, the main burner and/or the pilot turn off. The gas control knob stays where you left it, at PILOT or ON.

Getting it going again

You have to cycle the system by hand. Remove the safety screen and open the lower grille to reach the gas valve and knob, then follow the steps in Lighting the pilot.

This is a standard safety feature of the SIT Millivolt Pilot-on-Demand control system.

flames.title: What the flames should look like
flames.html:
When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes of operation they gradually turn yellow.

Ideal: lazy, yellow flames. No adjustment is needed. The flames should be steady, not lifting or floating.

Altitude, fuel quality and the venting setup all affect how the flames look, so a new installation may need further adjustment to look its best. The manual shows example flame pictures on this page.

Call a qualified service technician if the flames stay blue, turn dark orange with black tips (soot), or lift off the burner. Only a technician should adjust the burner's air (venturi) setting.

Soot on the glass can also come from logs placed over the burner ports. The technician checks the log positions before touching the air setting.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles on the floor.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The safety barrier that comes with the fireplace must be installed. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this appliance.
  • Supervise young children in the same room. If someone in the house is at risk, an adjustable safety gate can keep them away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace, along with gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Call a qualified service technician right away.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpeting or bedding can mean more frequent cleaning. The control compartments, burners and air passageways must be kept clean.

Firebox · service personAnnually
Fan · service personEvery 6 months
Vent system · service personAnnually
Burner & pilot · service personAnnually
Glass · you (and the service person)Annually

What the technician checks

  • Vacuums the firebox, fan and burner system. The fan's bearings are sealed and need no oiling.
  • Checks gas tubes and connections for leaks, and that the pilot flame reaches the thermocouple.
  • Confirms the main burner lights within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, and that the flame safety system responds in no more than 30 seconds.
  • Inspects the vent system, the glass and the bottom latches.
Any screen, guard or barrier removed for service must go back on before the fireplace runs again.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s limited lifetime warranty covers the original purchaser from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship.

30 days · parts & laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborAll other parts and material
Years 2 through lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory liner (not enamel or glass panels)
  • Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model. You don't need to send anything in to register.
  • If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days. Labor is reimbursed to authorized dealers only.

What voids it

  • Installation other than by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not following the manual.
  • Removing the serial number or testing label, or altering the appliance.
  • Submersion in water or long periods of dampness.
Not covered: chimney components and non-Hussong accessories, venting and other installation problems, and how well it heats your space.

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m).

Fuel conversion

Manufactured for natural gas and not convertible unless a certified kit is used: propane kit OCK-S53A, NG kit OCK-S42A (p. 40). Follow the kit's instructions and complete the conversion before installing the log set.

Propane11" WC min · 13" WC max

Table 12.1 (p. 34) gives the same values. Measure at the IN tap with all other gas appliances in the house on, or at full capacity.

Gas line

  • A listed (and Commonwealth of Massachusetts approved) ½ in. (13 mm) tee handle manual shut-off valve and flexible gas connector connect to the ½ in. (13 mm) control valve inlet. If substituting, check local codes.
  • Supplied: 3/8" (10 mm) x 18" (457 mm) long flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • Run the line in, preferably through the right gas line hole, without obstructing fan operation.
  • Tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At or below: close its manual shut-off valve.

specOpening.title: Minimum fireplace opening
specOpening.html:
(A) Height19-1/4" (489mm)
(B) Front width29-1/2" (749mm)
(C) Depth15" (381mm)
(D) Back width18-7/8" (479mm)

For a solid fuel masonry or factory-built non-combustible fireplace installed to code. Smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if attached by mechanical fasteners; remove firebrick if needed to reach the minimum opening. Cutting any sheet metal part of the existing fireplace is prohibited.

  • Set on a level surface able to support the insert and venting, and keep service access clearances.
  • If the metal floor is removed, set the insert directly on the metal base and mechanically attach the "This unit has been modified" label at the bottom of the existing firebox.
  • The gas line access hole is on the right side of the insert.

Overall appliance dimensions are shown only as a drawing (Figure 2.1, p. 9).

specChimney.title: Existing chimney
specChimney.html:
Masonry chimney6" x 8" (152mm x 203mm) min. inside diameter
Factory-built solid fuel chimney7" (178mm) min. inside diameter
Chimney height10' (3.05m) min · 50' (15.24m) max

The chimney must be non-combustible, clean and in good working order (p. 14), and must not share or connect to a flue serving any other appliance (p. 13). Remove and discard the existing chimney cap.

Liner length

With one person at the fireplace opening and one at the top of the chimney, measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney and subtract the height of the insert. That is the length of co-linear flexible aluminum pipe needed.

Where a chimney no longer terminates through the roofline, a co-linear to co-axial adapter may be installed where it ends. After the adapter, keep 1" (25mm) clearance to combustibles on all sides of the co-axial pipe.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Liner3" x 3" co-linear flex (exhaust + combustion air)
Kozy Heat #81636' (10.97 m) expandable 3" flexible pipe + round cap (#816-CAP)
Max horizontal run (3" x 3" flex)24"
Co-linear + co-axial total10' min · 50' max
Cap to intersecting walls, overhangs, eaves12" (305mm)

#816 is for minimum 6" x 8" I.D. masonry or 7" I.D. Class A metal chimneys. Other approved vent manufacturers: BDM, American Metals (Amerivent), Metal Fab, Olympia Venting Supply, Selkirk, Simpson Dura-Vent and ICC. The insert's exhaust collar is on the right and the exhaust pipe has a red marking; install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right.

Co-linear may be combined with co-axial venting using an approved 4" x 6-5/8" adapter. Minimum co-axial vertical termination height above the roof runs from 1.0 ft (flat to 6/12) to 8.0 ft (over 20/12 to 21/12) in Table 4.1 (p. 13), with 12" between two vertical terminations.

Note: pp. 15 and 16 say horizontal runs (24 in max) require a 1 in (25mm) rise per 12 in (305 mm) run; the troubleshooting chart on p. 37 says a pitch of ¼ in (6 mm) per 12 in (30 cm) is required on horizontal venting.

specClear.title: Clearances & mantels
specClear.html:
Adjacent sidewall6" (152mm) from appliance sides
Enclosure floor to ceiling55" (1.40m) min.
9" (229mm) combustible mantelStarts 16" (407mm) above top of appliance
6" (152mm) mantel with CK29-LMKStarts 11" (279mm) above top of appliance
Maker's website: its brochure gives mantel 9" deep: 16" from top of insert (11" with Low Mantel Kit). Install to the manual.

From either starting point, mantel depth may increase 1" for every 1" of added height. The CK29-LMK low mantel kit is for use only with safety barriers CK29-RSF and CK29-PSF. Combustible floor can be in front of and underneath the unit.

Proper safety barrier installation requires the bottom of the fireplace to be level with the finished hearth, so allow for the hearth finish when building a platform (p. 11).

The inch figures agree on every page. The manual also prints 55" as 1.04m and the 16" mantel height as 254mm (p. 22), and the 9" mantel as 254mm and 11" as 305mm (p. 23); the metric figures shown here are the ones it prints elsewhere (1.40m on pp. 23 and 25, 407mm on p. 23, 229mm and 279mm on pp. 22 and 25).

Outdoor covered installation (p. 19)

Operation is approved from 40°F to 110°F. The overhang in front, and to each side, must be at least 1/2 of the roofline elevation above the base of the fireplace. Black painted safety barriers are highly recommended outdoors.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Junction box120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps
Gas valveMillivolt; does not require 110-120 VAC
Optional controlsLow-voltage thermostat or wall switch
Maker's website: Ignition, Electronic Ignition Pilot System. This manual describes a millivolt gas valve system, with a pilot you light by hand using the piezo igniter button.

The AC supply must be hot at all times, with no switch installed in it. Shut off the household breaker before working on electrical lines. Ground the appliance per local codes or, without them, the National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 or the Canadian Electrical Code CSA C22.1. It has a three-prong grounding plug for a properly grounded three-prong receptacle.

Never connect high voltage (115V) wire to the gas valve. The optional component connection is for low voltage battery or direct current only, not 120 or 240 volts AC.

conflicts.issue: Horizontal vent pitch: pp. 15 and 16 require a 1 in (25mm) rise per 12 in (305 mm) run on horizontal runs (24 in max); the troubleshooting chart on p. 37 says ¼ in (6 mm) per 12 in (30 cm).

Venturi fix for blue, lifting flames: p. 35 says opening the air shutter causes a short blue flame that may lift off the burner and Table 12.3 says close slightly for short blue flames; the p. 37 chart says a flame that burns blue and lifts off the burner may need the venturi opened slightly.

Metric clearance values disagree (inch values agree): 55" = 1.04m (p. 22) vs 1.40m (pp. 23, 25); 16" = 254mm (p. 22) vs 407mm (p. 23); 9" = 229mm (pp. 22, 25) vs 254mm (p. 23); 11" = 279mm (pp. 22, 25) vs 305mm (p. 23).

review.notes: Millivolt configuration only (CSK-29-MV, manual R.10 April 2021). Ignition: hand-lit pilot with piezo igniter on a SIT millivolt valve; regions that require it get a 7 day time-out Pilot-on-Demand valve (p. 33; parts 700-086N-7 / 700-087A-7). Catalog MV BTU inputs (28,500/18,500 NG; 29,000/22,000 LP) match p. 8. The manual gives no efficiency, view area or heating area, so catalog AFUE and view area are unverified. Figure 2.1 (p. 9) lists 19¼", 29½" and 14½" among unlabeled dimensions, consistent with catalog H/W/D, but the text doesn't say which is which, so not transcribed or verified. Shown only as drawings and not transcribed: appliance dimensions (p. 9), safety barrier sizes (p. 11), wiring schematics (p. 31), low mantel kit assembly (p. 24), flame pictures (pp. 35, 39). The manual never says where the rocker switch or piezo button sits, and gives no fan controls or remote operating instructions (a remote is only mentioned on pp. 29 and 37), so the guide has no remote or fan tile. The lighting label says 'control compartment access panel' (p. 32); p. 33 says the gas valve and knob are reached by removing the safety screen and opening the lower grille, which the owner text uses. Minor, not flagged: kPa rounding differs between p. 8 and p. 34 (0.40 vs 0.41, 2.49 vs 2.48), so the guide shows in. WC only; 24 in = 609 mm (p. 15) vs 610mm (p. 16); chimney minimum 10' = 3.05m (p. 12) vs 3m (Fig. 3.2). Other oddities: the p. 39 flame drawing is labeled 'Honeywell millivolt pilot flame' while the valve is SIT (pp. 33, 40); p. 21 cites Section 3.2 'on page 19' (it is p. 12); the #816-CAP is (D) in the p. 15 figure but (E) in its steps. Gas line: p. 21 calls for a listed ½ in. tee handle shut-off and flexible connector to the ½ in. valve inlet and also lists a supplied 3/8" x 18" flexible connector; both shown as printed. Pages 2, 4, 6 and 42 carry no text (blank pages; QA warns on them). No LED/error code table, so codes is empty. Massachusetts sidewall-vent rules (p. 7) not summarized. No French-only or scrambled text needed decoding.
